steps.text: Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain.
In a Dutch oven, brown ground beef over medium heat. Add chopped onion, and cook until onion is soft. Add green pepper and tomato sauce; cook until pepper is soft.

raw_recipe.headline: Elbows and Ground Beef
raw_recipe.description: It's hard to go wrong with this effortless simmer of ground beef, sweet bell peppers and onions in a tomato sauce. Serve over macaroni and pass the cheese.
raw_recipe.name: Elbows and Ground Beef

recipeInstructions.text: Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain.
In a Dutch oven, brown ground beef over medium heat. Add chopped onion, and cook until onion is soft. Add green pepper and tomato sauce; cook until pepper is soft.

review.reviewBody: This is a basic macaroni and ground beef dish. I made some changes to the recipe. I seasoned the ground beef with salt, pepper and garlic powder to taste. I sauteed the onions and green pepper together. I only had 3-8oz cans of tomato sauce so I placed approximately one half can of diced tomatoes with green chilies in with the tomato sauce. I simmered this for a few minutes and then added the cooked macaroni. I didn't use the entire box of macaroni because I thought it would be too dry with the amount of sauce that I had. The addition of the canned tomatoes with green chilies gave it a fresher taste and added a little bite to it.A sprinkling of parmesean cheese on top and it is good to go. I served it with a Caesar salad and garlic bread. This made a very nice weekday dinner.I will definitely make this again and again. Thank you!

I agree with other posters that this is not the best meal I have ever had, but it is a great pull-together-from-what-you-usually-have-on-hand dinner. It reminded me of Hamburger Helper, but much better tasting without all the preservatives and junk. It actually was better than I expected and my husband gobbled it down. Some modifications that I made: #1 Only used 1 lb of ground turkey, #2 Used two cans of 8 oz tomato sauce (correction from two 14.5 oz) and one 14.5 oz can of diced tomatoes. #3 Did as other suggested and sauteed bell peppers, onion, and later garlic in a little bit of olive oil before adding the meat. #4 16 oz box of noodles is a bit much. I used probably about 2/3-3/4 of what I cooked and will do a mini mac and cheese with the rest. #5 Did this as a bake. Put everything in a 9x13 pan and baked until heated through and sauce was bubbling. Added a layer of cheese on top and put back in the oven for about 5 minutes until melted. Yummy!

Very good...memories from childhood...my Grammie called it Wash Day supper because it is easy and all in one pot. DO NOT USE SPAGHETTI SAUCE! Do not pre-cook the macaroni....just put it in the pot dry to soak up and cook in the tomato, pepper and beef juices. I used 1 can beef broth, 1 can tomato sauce and a can of condensed tomato soup, can of Rotel, jar of canned garden tomatoes from last year, garlic and a little Italian seasoning (1 tsp). Delicious and cheap meal. Used a potato masher to break up the ground beef.

My husband loved this. Followed other suggestions using what I had on hand-spaghetti sauce, garlic powder red pepper flakes, Rotel with chiles, mushrooms and Mexican cheese. Made me think of hamburger helper only way better. First time I tried cooking the pasta in the sauce rather than boiling. It had to cook longer but it worked! I just kept checking the tenderness of the pasta. followed another reviewer’s suggestion and

I added to this 8 sliced fresh mushrooms and added after onion & peppers were sautéed in olive oil added frozen corn and cooked on low heat for 5 mins substitute 1/2 the sauce with 15 1/2 oz can of diced tomatoes added elbow macaroni and seasoned with salt, pepper and garlic powered. My husband loves this

Great basic recipe. After reading all the reviews I used this recipe as a guideline. I added chopped celery and carrots. I used a red bell pepper. I used 1 28 oz can of crushed tomatoes and added water as needed to cook the noodles in the same pot (about 3/4 can). I also added chicken base. I seasoned everything as I added to the pot. I used salt, pepper, Italian herb mix, minced garlic and garlic powder, red pepper flakes. I only used 1lb ground beef and 8 oz pasta. I sautéed all the vegetables together then added the beef. Drained it all. Added the crushed tomatoes and pasta. Simmered until the pasta was cooked. Me and the hubby enjoyed it. Definitely easy and worth making again.

I browned my meat with the an onion, a green pepper, minced garlic, salt & pepper then after draining I added two 8 oz. cans of tomato sauce one can stewed tomatoes and a jar of my grandma's stewed tomatoes (because that all I had on hand) I then added a 16 oz box of rotini and brought it all to a boil, then simmered it until the pasta was tender. I added colby jack on top to melt and my family liked it alot. Next time I will use the 2 cans tomato sauce and 3 cans of stewed tomatoes. Hope this helps. Thanks for the recipe.

Great recipe I did modify to make it my own. For starters I cooked 5 pieces of bacon in dutch oven used the grease to cook garlic, onion and peppers. In addition, I used 16 oz crushed tomatoes, 12 oz tomato sauce, 1 Tbsp. red hot and 1 Tbsp soy sauce. After mixing all together I put it in oven with crumpled cheddar cheese on top. Delish and I have leftovers for lunches.
This is similar to a recipe we call goulash. Some canned tomatoes, worchestershire sauce, and add a little extra liquid (water, broth, beer???j, then cook the pasta right in the same pot. Try it!

A lot of these recipes call for tomato sauce, which is a salty, unappetizing tomato product. Whole tomatoes would be a much better choice. You would get the sweetness of the tomatoes and less salt. The recipe calls for no real seasoning. Some garlic powder and some light Italian seasonings plus salt and pepper would give you a real dish.

I've been making this for years and years except I add either some fresh minced garlic or powdered garlic (whichever I have on hand)to my ground beef, bell peppers and onions while browning. I also add one to two cans of diced tomatoes including the juice instead of using tomato sauce after draining my ground beef then salt and pepper to taste. Add your noodles or macaroni last, stir and simmer until pasta is done. It's also good with a can of whole kernel corn added to it. This dish is good but we like my version a bit better.

This is a very basic recipe that uses bare minimum pantry staples. Perfect for a busy night or for the night when you’re at the end of your groceries. Could it be amped up a bit with spices? Absolutely! But that’s the joy of a basic recipe. The flavor profile can be changed each time you make it.

A comfort food in my house which we love. Easy to make and my family enjoyed it. I used 1 pound of ground beef which I think is plenty for the recipe.I think it needs some seasoning, so I added the following: I added 1 teaspoon of garlic powder, 1 teaspoon of onion powder, 1 teaspoon of garlic salt, 2 minced garlic cloves, and 1/4 teaspoon of black pepper.

This was a very easy recipe to make but it lacked flavor. I even added a tablespoon of Red Pepper Flakes but it still was missing something. Also, two cans of 29 ounce tomato sauce is an overkill. We used one 24 ounce of pasta sauce and another 15 ounce can of tomato sauce and that was still too much. I'd used one 24-ounce jar of pasta sauce. That would likely suffice. I won't be making this again.
I made it but added some Italian seasoning and diced tomatoes which made it really good.
So good everyone went back for seconds

Overall it's good. Needs to be jazzed up some for my taste. I substituted a can of Rotell for the bell pepper and used several shots of worcester sauce. This did make a difference. Fast, easy to make ,and clean up was not bad. I will make this again.

Basic recipe for sure. You need add some spices such as chili powder, garlic, etc. Also if you add tomato sauce, I always add a little brown sugar to kill the acid on it. Top with some cheese such as Monterey jack. Dress it up so it has some taste.
I made this recipe all the time. Thank you
Way too much for two people. I would use half amounts of meat, tomato sauce and pasta.
